newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian late palm olein hit by USDA report.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian late palm olein hit by USDA report.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were weaker in late trading on Monday in line with a plunge in soyoil prices in Chicago following the release of bearish U.S. soybean production figures by the USDA, traders said.
They said olein was around 1,380-90 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, compared with 1,390-95 rupiah at the opening. One player was heard offering small quantities at 1,370-75 rupiah.

The decline comes in the wake of the release last Friday of a USDA report showing 1996 U.S. soybean production totalling 2.346 billion bushels, well above trade expections and a September USDA forecast for 2.270 billion.
"I had no choice but to cut prices," one trader with a major plantation house said. "The USDA report and its impact on soyoil prices in Chicago is pushing down palm oil prices."
The report triggered a sharp fall in Malaysian prices.
Traders said the already weak sentiment in the local market, where prices have been declining steadily the last three weeks, had been further dampened by the USDA report.
"I see a further downside in local prices," one trader said. "Some players have begun to sell aggresively and others are chasing these prices."
